You’ll leave your hotel for the railway station and take a tourist train to Machu Picchu. High in the mountains, an entire city of stone buildings, terraces and plazas has survived. An American explorer came across it in the 20th century, after which Machu Picchu became one of South America’s best-known archaeological sites.

On the guided tour, you’ll walk through the ancient city and see the surrounding mountains and deep canyons. Afterwards, you’ll have free time to take photos and explore on your own. With luck, you may spot llamas nearby.

You’ll then take the bus down to the village for lunch at Ayasqa restaurant. After lunch, you’ll head to the station for the return train journey and transfer to your hotel in Cusco.
Stone church with two towers beside a square with benches in Cusco, Peru
Cusco: church façade, street lamps and people walking through the square

After breakfast, you’ll set out on a guided tour of the Sacred Valley. Its fertile soil and favourable climate made it an important agricultural centre of the Inca civilisation.

The route takes you through Urubamba, where the Inca ruler Huayna Capac had a country residence. In Pisac, a large archaeological complex sits on Vilcabamba Hill, and its layout is associated with the shape of a partridge. Ollantaytambo is known for its ceremonial centre. In Chinchero, a colonial church still stands above the walls of the Inca Temple of the Sun. You’ll also stop at Moray, where agricultural terraces form a vast amphitheatre.

Near Pisac, you can visit a market and browse silverwork, pottery and leather goods made by local artisans. At the Awana Kancha animal centre, you’ll see llamas, alpacas and vicuñas and learn how they are raised and how their prized wool is traditionally dyed.

Overnight in the Sacred Valley.
